candidate.title: The Optimal Bound for Non-Adaptive DDH with Preprocessing
candidate.subtitle: The square-root term in the proved bound is an artefact for DDH but not for square-DDH
candidate.one_line: A non-adaptive (S,T)-algorithm for DDH in the generic group model succeeds with probability at most 1/2 + O~(T^2/N + ST/N), rather than the proved 1/2 + O~(T^2/N + sqrt(ST/N)).
candidate.informal: Preprocessing helps an attacker distinguish Diffie-Hellman keys from random, and how much depends on whether its queries may react to each other. The source paper proves that a non-adaptive attacker with S bits of advice and T queries does no better than 1/2 + O~(T^2/N + sqrt(ST/N)), and shows that for the square variant of the problem that is exactly right, with a matching attack. For plain DDH it believes its own square-root term is an artefact of combining two bounds, and that the truth is 1/2 + O~(T^2/N + ST/N).
candidate.status_note: Open. The proved bound is the source's Theorem 1.2; the conjectured improvement is stated twice, in the results section and again in the open-problems paragraph. The same theorem's bound for square-DDH is sharp, with an attack the source sketches in its Appendix B.
candidate.progress_note: The source names the route it expects to work: combining the techniques of Akshima-Besselman-Guo-Xie-Ye, who settled the adaptive case at 1/2 + Theta~(ST^2/N), with its own. Nothing has been published in that direction.

candidate.why_interesting: It is a gap the source can locate exactly: the same theorem is sharp for square-DDH and believed lossy for DDH, so whatever separates the two problems is invisible to the current proof. Settling it finishes the non-adaptive picture for the three standard generic-group problems.
candidate.why_clean: Both the proved and the conjectured bound are explicit formulas in the source, and the model is fully specified there.
candidate.risks: The source says 'the optimal bound is', which claims a matching algorithm as well; the page states only the upper-bound half and says so. Check whether the corresponding non-adaptive attack really achieves ST/N -- if it does not, the source's two-sided sentence is false even if this statement is true.
candidate.formal_statement_latex: There is a function $c(\cdot)$, polylogarithmic in $N$, such that for every prime $N$ and every non-adaptive $(S,T)$-algorithm for DDH in the generic group model over a group of order $N$, the success probability is at most $1/2 + c(N) \cdot (T^{2}/N + ST/N)$.

verify.reason: The conjecture is stated twice in the source, in its own words, with the value named; it is not proved anywhere, and its Section 5.2 proves only the weaker Theorem 1.2. The correction that mattered: the source's phrase 'the optimal bound is' asserts a matching lower bound too, and the first draft folded both halves into one statement without recording the choice.

checks.name: existence
checks.finding: Printed on printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6) immediately after Theorem 1.2, and again in the open-problems paragraph on printed p. 10 (PDF p. 11).

checks.name: openness
checks.finding: Listed as an open problem; Section 5.2 proves only Theorem 1.2, whose DDH case the source calls not tight. No later result improves it.

checks.name: strength
checks.finding: 'the optimal bound is X' claims both an upper bound and a matching attack. The page states the upper-bound half only, which is weaker than the source's sentence; recorded explicitly in the setting and in a remark rather than silently.

checks.name: quantifiers-and-parameters
checks.finding: N prime; success probability measured against 1/2 as in Theorem 1.2; the polylogarithmic factor is the source's O~. The DDH query structure is quoted from the game definition on PDF p. 18.

checks.name: attribution
checks.finding: The conjecture is the source's own; the adaptive tight bound is attributed to [ABG+24] and the earlier upper bound and the sqDDH attack to [CK18], as in the source.

checks.name: definitions
checks.finding: The DDH permutation-challenge game, including the translation function for k = 0 and k = 1, is reproduced from the source's Section 3.3.

checks.name: fabrication
checks.finding: The remark contrasting the degree structure of DDH and square-DDH queries is derived from the two translation functions printed in the source, and is labelled as this page's reading of why the proof cannot tell them apart.

checks.name: self-containment
checks.finding: The model, the game and both bounds are on the page.

corrections.problem: Stated the source's 'optimal bound' as if the matching-attack half were also being conjectured.
corrections.corrected: State the upper-bound half only, and record the two-sided reading in a remark with what a solver should check.

corrections.problem: Did not record that the same theorem is sharp for square-DDH.
corrections.corrected: Say so, since it is what makes the DDH case a question rather than a suspicion.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Proving time-space lower bounds for adaptive attacks with preprocessing for the other problems the paper treats -- square-DDH and Even-Mansour -- as a function of the number of adaptivity rounds (printed p. 10).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: The source poses the r-round goal 'for the problems considered in this paper' but names a conjectured formula only for DLOG and, separately, an improved bound for DDH. For sqDDH and EM there is no proposition to publish, only the goal.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Extending the proof technique to challenge-dependent pre-translated queries (printed p. 10).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: A technique-development goal, not a proposition: the source says it 'would require new Shearer-type inequalities or alternative techniques'. It is recorded as the obstruction on c/0060 instead.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Proving slightly super-linear time-space lower bounds for oblivious branching programs, which the source says its motivating question is related to (printed p. 4, footnote 2).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: A 30-year-old open problem in complexity theory that the source cites rather than poses, attributed to the line of work after Babai-Nisan-Szegedy. Not this paper's to leave open.
